Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Start with canonical driver, paralog, and stress-pathway hypotheses across the supplied lung cancer cell lines. Because more negative CRISPR dependency scores mean stronger dependency, I set direction -1 for hypotheses expecting stronger dependency in the exposed subgroup and direction +1 for hypotheses expecting weaker dependency. KRAS mutation and BRAF V600E should show selective dependency on the mutated gene if those models are addicted to the pathway. EGFR and ERBB2 amplifications may similarly mark lineages with increased dependency on the amplified receptor tyrosine kinase, though amplification can also be passenger. BAF-complex inactivation is expected to create paralog dependency on SMARCA2, so I test both SMARCA4 loss and ARID1A loss. TP53 loss should reduce MDM2 dependency because the MDM2-p53 axis is less relevant when p53 is absent; USP7 is expected to follow a similar, though less established, direction if p53 is not required. MSI-high lineages are tested for WRN selective dependency. KEAP1 loss is tested against NFE2L2 dependency because oxidative-stress-pathway activation can create selective pathway dependency. I also add an interaction for KRAS dependency between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma lung lineages to assess whether KRAS addiction is concentrated in the histologic subtype enriched for KRAS mutations. Finally, a broad sex comparison for STAT3 is registered as a low-prior but biologically plausible screen for population-level differences or confounding; the expected direction is uncertain. All first-wave comparisons are left unresolved pending estimates, uncertainty, and whether absolute dependency-score differences are meaningful relative to outcome variability and the 10% clinical relevance threshold.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The newly delivered validation resolves H3 negatively for the claim of a clinically meaningful predictor association. H3 predicted EGFR-amplified lineages to have stronger EGFR dependency; because the hypothesis direction was -1, the signed estimates are positive when they support stronger dependency. Discovery R3 gave a signed effect of +0.0252, only about the absolute 10% threshold for dependency_EGFR (approximately 0.025 given the mean score magnitude of 0.25), and its 95% interval crossed zero. Independent validation R13 was weaker: signed +0.0152, below the 10% threshold, and its stricter validation interval also crossed zero. Taken together, the evidence does not support EGFR amplification as a clinically meaningful predictor of EGFR dependency in this dataset. I therefore reject H3 and close it as a negative finding, while acknowledging that intervals are wide enough that smaller or context-dependent effects are not definitively excluded. I also reject H7: the TP53-loss effect on MDM2 was signed +0.0088, far below the approximately 0.027 absolute threshold for dependency_MDM2, and its interval was compatible with no difference. In contrast, H13 should be accepted. The same strong evidence that rejected H10 supports the reversed association: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with a signed estimate of +0.796 and an extremely tight interval. Thus the original KEAP1-to-stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected, but the opposite dataset association is accepted. The current dataset-supported associations are large and precise for SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These are not causal claims. The next priority is specificity and within-dataset robustness. H14-H17 already registered POLR2A negative-control tests for KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss; these are crucial because POLR2A is a broadly essential transcriptional machinery gene and should not be strongly associated with pathway-specific dependencies unless there is global screen-level confounding or a general bias. The new proposals H18-H21 test whether the accepted effects are stable across lung lineage_subtype adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma subgroups. These subtype interactions do not retest whether the effects exist, but they ask whether the effects are concentrated in one histologic context or are internally robust across available lung subtypes. I will downgrade accepted associations if POLR2A negative controls are positive, and I will narrow interpretation of accepted associations if subtype interactions are large despite stable main effects. All conclusions remain limited to the supplied dataset, without causal or external generalizability claims.

record.narrative: No assessments are due because the current pending claims H14-H21 have no new evidence yet. I register four additional mechanistic comparisons that extend the current plan without duplicating the accepted claims, the POLR2A specificity controls, or the adenocarcinoma-complement interactions already registered. The first wave and its synthesis show that the large dataset-supported associations are SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency, MSI-high stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These are now supported in the supplied dataset but remain noncausal and not yet specificity-controlled beyond the pending H14-H21 tests. For the new round, I choose predictors and outcomes that are biologically plausible but not yet tested. First, MYC amplification may create increased reliance on USP7 because USP7 stabilizes MYC and related oncogenic proteins; therefore MYC-amplified cells could show stronger, more negative USP7 dependency. Second, BRCA2 loss may expose dependency on alternative DNA repair or transcription-associated helicase mechanisms; I test stronger DHX9 dependency in BRCA2-loss cells. Third, PIK3CA mutation constitutively activates the PI3K/AKT pathway downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases, so PIK3CA-mutant cells may be less dependent on upstream EGFR, giving a less negative EGFR dependency score. Fourth, RB1 loss disrupts cell-cycle restraint and may increase sensitivity to mitotic machinery perturbations, so RB1-loss cells may show stronger dependency on KIF18A. All four are registered as unresolved and will be judged against the signed 95% Welch intervals, cell counts, and the 10% clinical-relevance rule on the dependency-score scale. If MYC amplification shows an USP7 effect, a POLR2A or other broad-essential specificity control should be registered in the next round. Similarly, if BRCA2 or RB1 effects appear large, follow-up should test whether they are outcome-specific or global screen effects. These proposals are exploratory associations only, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new results are signed to each claim direction, so positive estimates support the registered hypothesis and negative estimates oppose it. I judged each result against a 10% clinically relevant threshold on the outcome scale, using the absolute mean dependency score as the reference because the dependency scores are negative-centered. For the POLR2A specificity controls H14-H17, the signed contrasts are tiny: 0.0071, 0.0035, 0.0050, and -0.0140. The POLR2A absolute mean is about 0.255, so a 10% reference difference is about 0.0255. None of the point estimates approaches the threshold, every interval includes zero, and multiplicity across 12 discovery tests argues against treating borderline interval endpoints as meaningful. These null POLR2A contrasts support outcome specificity of the earlier large associations rather than a global screen-level association; therefore I reject H14-H17 as claims that these predictors are associated with clinically meaningful POLR2A dependency differences. For the adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma interaction checks H18-H21, the signed interaction estimates are small relative to their outcome scales and all intervals cross zero. H18 has estimate -0.028 versus a SMARCA2 reference threshold of about 0.042; H19 has estimate -0.010, slightly above the very small USP7 absolute-mean threshold but in the opposite direction with a wide interval; H20 has estimate -0.021 versus WRN threshold 0.030; H21 has estimate -0.012 in the opposite direction for NFE2L2 with a wide interval. There is not reliable evidence of clinically meaningful subtype-specific attenuation or concentration of the main effects, so I reject the registered interaction claims and do not narrow the accepted main associations. H22 remains the only borderline candidate: MYC amplification versus USP7 has signed estimate +0.026, which exceeds the roughly 0.0093 10% absolute-mean threshold for USP7, but the interval -0.018 to 0.071 includes zero and the result arises in a multiple-testing context. I therefore leave H22 unresolved and request independent validation. The remaining new comparisons H23-H25 are not clinically meaningful: BRCA2 loss/DHX9 estimate 0.012 against about 0.025 threshold, PIK3CA mutation/EGFR estimate -0.003 against about 0.025 threshold, and RB1 loss/KIF18A estimate 0.008 against about 0.026 threshold. All intervals include zero. I reject these as unsupported. Overall, the evidence supports the existing large dataset-specific associations but suggests no global POLR2A confounding, no meaningful adenocarcinoma subtype interaction, and no strong new associations except the unconfirmed MYC-USP7 candidate.

record.narrative: H22 tested whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger USP7 dependency in the supplied dataset. The original hypothesis direction was negative, so positive signed estimates support stronger dependency in MYC-amplified lineages. Discovery R22 gave a signed effect of +0.0264 with a 95% interval from -0.0181 to +0.0709. Using the same convention as prior appraisal, the clinically relevant threshold is 10% of the absolute mean outcome; for dependency_USP7 this is about 0.0093. The discovery point estimate exceeded that threshold, but the interval included zero and was wide, so the result was a borderline non-replicated candidate rather than a supported claim. Independent validation R26 was essentially null: signed +0.00016 with an interval from -0.0671 to +0.0675. The validation estimate is far below the 10% threshold, and the point estimate does not corroborate the discovery direction. The adjusted validation interval remains wide and therefore does not exclude all clinically meaningful positive or negative effects, but the total evidence does not support the proposed predictor association. I therefore reject H22 and close it as a negative dataset-specific finding: MYC amplification is not supported as a clinically meaningful predictor of USP7 dependency here. This leaves the main supported associations unchanged. The four large, precise dataset associations are accepted as supplied-dataset findings, not causal or externally generalizable claims. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5, signed estimate +0.784. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H8, signed estimate +0.802. MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H9, signed estimate +0.790. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H13, signed estimate +0.796. Each far exceeds its outcome-specific 10% threshold and has tight intervals excluding zero and the threshold. The current evidence also supports outcome and context specificity for these main effects in the tested sense. POLR2A negative-control tests did not show clinically meaningful differences for KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, or TP53 loss, arguing against a global screen-level confounder. Adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma interaction tests for the four accepted associations were null, so the available histologic-subgroup robustness is consistent with not narrowing the main effects. Other negative findings include EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, TP53 loss with MDM2 dependency, BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency, PIK3CA mutation with EGFR dependency, RB1 loss with KIF18A dependency, and the now-resolved MYC-USP7 candidate. The most informative next analyses are: first, a second broad-essential specificity control using RPL11 for the same four predictors; second, robustness checks of the accepted associations across culture type, especially adherent versus non-adherent subgroups; and third, an exploratory screen of research marker D against the four accepted outcomes. These follow-ups test whether the accepted dataset associations are selectively outcome-specific, stable across culture context, and whether an additional measured binary assay carries meaningful association. They do not change the accepted claims unless new evidence is large, precise, and consistent with clinical relevance.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The current evidence also supports outcome and context specificity for these main effects in the tested sense. Adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma interaction tests for the four accepted associations were null, so the available histologic-subgroup robustness is consistent with not narrowing the main effects. Other negative findings include EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, TP53 loss with MDM2 dependency, BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency, PIK3CA mutation with EGFR dependency, RB1 loss with KIF18A dependency, and the now-resolved MYC-USP7 candidate. The most informative next analyses are: first, a second broad-essential specificity control using RPL11 for the same four predictors; second, robustness checks of the accepted associations across culture type, especially adherent versus non-adherent subgroups; and third, an exploratory screen of research marker D against the four accepted outcomes. record.narrative: All returned estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I judged them against a 10% clinically meaningful threshold on the outcome scale, using the absolute mean dependency score as the reference, as in earlier appraisals. The RPL11 specificity controls H26-H29 are not supported as clinically meaningful associations: signed estimates are +0.0184, +0.0037, -0.0158, and +0.0163, with 95% intervals crossing zero and observed contrasts at or below the relevant RPL11 threshold of roughly 0.025. Some upper interval bounds remain above the threshold, so these controls do not prove exact nullity, but they do not support the registered positive-direction claims, especially in a multiple-discovery context. They therefore reinforce outcome specificity of the earlier large associations rather than global RPL11 screen-assay confounding. For culture-type interactions H30-H33, H30, H31, and H33 are not supported: H30 estimate +0.0145 for SMARCA2, H31 estimate -0.0024 for USP7, and H33 estimate -0.0187 for NFE2L2, all with intervals crossing zero and no reliable evidence for adherent-specific attenuation or concentration. This suggests that the MSI-high associated stronger WRN dependency is relatively stronger in adherent cultures than in the non-adherent complement within this supplied dataset. record.narrative:
Assessment of due validation: For H3, dependency_EGFR has mean -0.2495, so the 10% relevance threshold is about 0.025. Discovery R3 was borderline: signed estimate +0.0252 with a 95% interval crossing zero. Independent validation R13 was much weaker and imprecise: signed estimate +0.0152, adjusted interval -0.0254 to +0.0558. The validation point estimate is below the clinical-relevance threshold and does not corroborate a clinically meaningful stronger EGFR dependency in EGFR-amplified lineages in this dataset. Although the wide validation interval does not prove exact nullity, the total evidence does not support the registered association, so H3 is rejected and closed. For H5, dependency_SMARCA2 has mean -0.4155, threshold about 0.0415. Discovery R5 gave a huge signed effect of +0.784, and independent validation R39 gave +0.7857 with a lower bound of +0.7566 under the adjusted validation interval. Both are far above the 10% threshold and exclude near-null values, so H5 is accepted and closed as a robust dataset-specific association.

Current supported findings in the supplied lung panel: SMARCA4 loss is strongly associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated by R39. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; these remain accepted on discovery evidence and are highly precise, though H8, H9, and H13 have not yet shown the same independent validation status as H5. The accepted culture interaction H32 remains provisional because the non-adherent MSI-high exposed cell count is small (29), even though the signed interaction +0.1046 exceeded the threshold and its lower bound was above the threshold.

Negative or unsupported findings include overall KRAS mutation/KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification/EGFR dependency after validation, ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency, BRAF V600E/BRAF dependency, TP53 loss/MDM2 dependency, MYC amplification/USP7 dependency after validation, BRCA2 loss/DHX9 dependency, PIK3CA mutation/EGFR dependency, RB1 loss/KIF18A dependency, and the POLR2A and RPL11 specificity-control tests. Adenocarcinoma and culture-type interaction tests were mostly null except the H32 WRN interaction. These negative results argue against global screen confounding for the accepted effects but do not prove absence of context-specific effects.

Unresolved uncertainty includes independent validation of H32, independent confirmation for H8, H9, and H13, batch effects in H42-H45, and the pending research-marker D comparisons. The accepted effects are large but remain associations in this dataset, not causal claims or generalizable biological conclusions. The most informative next analyses are: validate H32 if not already cached; if that is not the best validation target, validate one of the accepted main effects or the next high-priority MYC candidate after discovery. The newly registered proposals focus on scientifically meaningful candidate dependencies: MYC amplification with KIF18A and RPL11, context-specific EGFR dependency in KRAS-wild-type lineages, and STK11 loss in the NFE2L2 pathway. These should be interpreted with the same 10% absolute-mean threshold, cell-count validity, and interval-based reasoning.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No discovery or validation evidence is currently due, so no accept/reject changes are made. I defer the four research-marker D claims because marker D is an arbitrary binary assay with no assigned gene or pathway and therefore should not displace molecularly anchored comparisons when analysis capacity is limited. The new proposals are grouped into three scientifically useful tracks. First, I test the unassessed RIT1 dependency outcome against KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, and BRAF V600E. RIT1 is an oncogenic RAS-pathway activator, so these comparisons ask whether RIT1 dependency is altered by canonical upstream or downstream MAPK drivers; the registered direction is weaker RIT1 dependency in driver-positive lineages, but the prior is genuinely uncertain and results could support the opposite direction. Second, I refine prior targeted-dependency findings by context: KRAS dependency in TP53-loss and STK11-loss contexts, EGFR dependency in a mutually exclusive driver-negative EGFR-amplified setting, and BRAF dependency in STK11-intact lineages. These test whether prior overall nulls or weak effects become meaningful in biologically defined subsets rather than globally. Third, I probe boundary conditions for the accepted large associations using MYC amplification as an oncogenic replication-stress modifier: interactions of MYC amplification with SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2, TP53 loss for USP7, and KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2, plus a new MYC amplification versus WRN main effect. I also test whether the accepted KEAP1-NFE2L2 association persists after excluding STK11 loss. All proposals will be judged against the 10% absolute-mean threshold, 95% Welch intervals, and at least 20 observations per cell. This stage does not claim causality or external generalizability; it registers dataset-specific, falsifiable comparisons for later discovery analysis.
